input: scheduled: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products (ventures brief)
task: Deepen (flagship 7) photo-editing: Pentax lens numbers and PENTAX private data

doc_friction.issue: Running a downloaded ExifTool checkout as a reference decoder was refused by the auto-mode classifier (untrusted download); the runbooks don't say to use a tool's checked-in test outputs (ExifTool t/*.out) as truth instead, which worked.

The numpy engine copies lens fields onto its report in a separate line (report.lens, report.lens_notes = ...) from the pure-Python DevelopReport; a new report field set in one path silently stays None in the other. Cost one test round.

deviations.why: The natural reading is to map Pentax numbers to lens names, but the only full table is ExifTool's own compilation (Artistic/GPL) and a number is not always one lens (3 44 = any Sigma or Tamron).
deviations.did: Read the numbers and lens codes, and added a per-photographer lens memory (--lens-memory) keyed by the body's number instead of shipping a name table; it also resolves Canon range ties.
deviations.result: 4 of 7 real Pentax frames go from refused to corrected (the 645D and Q-S1 lenses have no lensfun profile) with one --lens per lens; no third-party table in the tree.

notes: Verification: python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py photo-editing -> ok (148.8s), 1 suite, 0 failed. tests/test_pentax_lens.py 12 passed. Real files (metadata-extractor-images K-1 Mark II PEF/JPEG, 645D, *ist D, Q-S1 JPEG/DNG; ExifTool t/images/Pentax.jpg K10D): K10D decode = ExifTool t/Pentax_2.out (3 44, 10.0 mm, 4.0, 3.9); LC8 focal = EXIF focal on all others (77.5 vs 77 on *ist D, LC8 step). Post checks: frontmatter ok, 0 broken links, 0 similar pairs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: format research, reader for 5 LensInfo layouts, lens memory through CLI/pipeline, tests and real-file eval
